abstract: We establish a connection between the quasi-adiabatic propagator path integral (QuAPI) method and fast resummation of Dyson series (FRODS). Building on this connection, we introduce a path integral method with far-field expansion (PIFFE) for quantum systems coupled linearly to a thermal Gaussian bath. PIFFE combines QuAPI with a Taylor expansion of the far-field bath influence, keeping interactions within $r$ time steps in exponential form. The scheme has error $O(Δt^2)$ at fixed final time and is free of stochastic or tensor-compression errors. Spin-boson tests show that PIFFE gives results much closer to QuAPI than FRODS does, even for small $r$, while requiring substantially less storage than QuAPI. This allows much longer bath memory lengths and simulations of multilevel systems. Truncating the bath memory and limiting the total auxiliary degree further reduce storage and computational costs.
